statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-70354 (GHSA-gg8c-3338-xw2f) is an out-of-bounds write in Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF) that lets an attacker execute code locally. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and the Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime packs for win-x64, win-x86 and win-arm64 as the only affected .NET 10 packages, affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.10 and fixed in 10.0.11 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gg8c-3338-xw2f, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/432, https://github.com/dotnet/wpf/issues/11828, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.11/10.0.11.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's dotnet/dotnet source release, and each build's version is the .NET release it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. No WPF code is present: there is no PresentationFramework, PresentationCore, PresentationUI, System.Xaml, ReachFramework, DirectWriteForwarder, UIAutomation, wpfgfx, PresentationNative or PenImc assembly or native library, and no Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App shared framework or runtime pack. What the packages hold for Windows desktop development is build-time material, metadata and documentation: the WindowsBase.dll compatibility facade (6 KB) that ships with the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework and its runtime, NativeAOT and reference packs, a type-forwarding facade with no WPF code; the PresentationBuildTasks MSBuild task and the other Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WindowsDesktop build files (in the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap and in a nupkg in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts), which compile XAML at build time and are not the WPF runtime; the WPF and Windows Forms project template packages (Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf.ProjectTemplates and Microsoft.Dotnet.WinForms.ProjectTemplates) in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts and in the templates folder of the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, which hold only template project, XAML and source files and package metadata; the Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Ref and Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Internal nupkg files in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, which hold only package metadata and no assemblies; the Microsoft.Private.Winforms nupkg in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, which holds MSBuild props and targets for Windows Forms projects besides its package metadata; IntelliSense documentation XML files for the Windows desktop APIs (among them PresentationFramework.xml, PresentationCore.xml and System.Xaml.xml) in the Microsoft.Private.Intellisense package in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, which hold no code; the Microsoft.Internal.Runtime.WindowsDesktop.Transport nupkg in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, which carries libraries built in the .NET runtime repository (such as System.Security.Cryptography.Xml and System.IO.Packaging) and no WPF assembly; and debug symbol files: WindowsBase.pdb beside the facade (in dotnet10-runtime-dbg and in the shared framework and NativeAOT pack held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap), PresentationBuildTasks.pdb beside the build task, and symbols for WindowsBase, PresentationBuildTasks and Microsoft.Private.Winforms in the symbols archive held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap. None of the packages contains a native Windows PE file or a Mach-O file; every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly. So the vulnerable WPF code is not in this owner.

CVE-2026-70354 (GHSA-gg8c-3338-xw2f) is an out-of-bounds write in Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF) that allows local code execution. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime (win-*) as the only affected .NET 9 package, fixed in 9.0.19 (https://github.com/dotnet/wpf/security/advisories/GHSA-gg8c-3338-xw2f, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/432, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.19/9.0.19.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: none of them contains the Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App runtime or any WPF or Windows Forms assembly (PresentationCore, PresentationFramework, System.Xaml, System.Windows.Forms and the like), and none contains a native Windows PE file. WPF names appear only as IntelliSense XML documentation files in Microsoft.Private.Intellisense reference packages in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts, a Microsoft.Internal.Runtime.WindowsDesktop.Transport package in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts holds runtime libraries such as System.Security.Cryptography.Xml and System.Diagnostics.EventLog and no WPF or Windows Forms assembly, and WindowsBase.dll appears only as the .NET compatibility facade in the .NET shared framework and its runtime, ILCompiler and reference packs, not the WPF implementation.
